reconcile.connective: Older harmonists read Matthew's and Mark's witnesses as garbling, not inventing, the very saying John reports Jesus making at the temple.

discrepancy.connective: The early critic K. G. Bretschneider pressed the opposite reading: since the synoptists themselves call the witnesses false, Jesus never spoke John's words at all.

skeptic.name: Karl Gottlieb Bretschneider
skeptic.work: Probabilia de Evangelii et Epistolarum Joannis Apostoli indole et origine
skeptic.attribution: Karl Gottlieb Bretschneider, Probabilia de Evangelii et Epistolarum Joannis Apostoli indole et origine (1820)

excerpts.excerpt_text: …he did not say, "I am able to destroy the temple", but only said, "destroy this temple" … and so they perverted his sense, as well as misquoted his words …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill treats the trial testimony as a garbling of the exact wording of John 2:19, not an invented saying, arguing the witnesses perverted Jesus' sense while misquoting his words.

excerpts.excerpt_text: False witnesses giving false testimony misrepresented what Jesus said about the destruction and rebuilding of the Temple (see 15:29; John 2:19; Acts 6:14).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: States directly that the 'false' testimony at trial was a misrepresentation of what Jesus actually said in John 2:19, i.e. the same saying, distorted rather than fabricated.

excerpts.excerpt_text: …this figurative speech used here proved such a stumbling-block to them that it was produced in evidence against him at his trial to prove him a blasphemer.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Deep within Henry's block comment on John 2, this sentence identifies the saying at the trial (Matt 26:60-61) as the same figurative speech Jesus used at the temple cleansing, not a separate slander.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), comment on Matthew 26:60
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill's note on Matthew 26:60 (excerpted above) is a full PD harmonization of this exact contradiction, arguing the false witnesses garbled rather than invented what Jesus said in John 2:19.
